verifier_note: Checked against: the WebAssembly Core Spec (numerics/values/profiles/instruction-index pages), RFC 3514, Rust std docs and two Rust blog posts, five rust-lang/rust files fetched raw at tag 1.98.1 (one WebFetch summary inverted a cfg's boolean logic on compiler-builtins/src/math/mod.rs and had to be re-derived from a direct curl of the same URL), the pinned crate sources for rapier3d-f64/parry3d-f64/simba/glam/glamx/indexmap/hashbrown/foldhash/wide/libm read from the local cargo registry checkout (byte-identical to what docs.rs mirrors), si-rpg-engine's solver/src/lib.rs, solver/src/rapier_law.rs, solver/FLAGS.md, solver/Cargo.toml, solver/rust-toolchain.toml and solver/build.mjs fetched from GitHub main, and four of my own compile_oracle.py counter-example runs (E0015, E0599, E0658, algebraic_mul/algebraic_add) that all reproduced exactly what the checks claim. Nothing was refuted: every warrant resolved and supported its claim, every quoted engine fact matched the live repository (several verbatim, including js_min/js_max reproduced character-for-character and canonicalize_zero's real call sites on rapier3d-f64's warm-start impulses), and none of my own falsification attempts broke a recipe. The one systemic weakness is in recipe 8's engine_note: its most striking claim, that solver_step's compiled wasm actually reaches parry's BVH optimizer and glamx's eigensolver through a specific call chain, is a one-time, unrepeated wasmparser measurement on a scratch build, asserted at the same confidence as the fully source-grounded claims around it, and none of the lane's own checks re-verify that reachability (they verify wasm-vs-libm digest matching, an adjacent but weaker fact). A future dependency bump could silently break that specific claim with nothing in checks[] positioned to catch it.
